sectors.trend: Mixed: iron ore downside pressures majors, but WA gold and rare earths show strong exploration momentum. Forrestania four prefeasibility studies, Dalaroo Greenland rare earths, Larvotto antimony-gold first concentrate, Great Southern 10.72g/t gold results.
sectors.implications: Rotation from iron ore (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) toward gold (GOLD.AX, NVC.AX) and critical minerals (DAR.AX, LRV.AX, FRT.AX). Iron ore weakness caps large-cap mining upside.

sectors.trend: Super contributions surge >33% post-budget; digital pension scheme proposed; super system criticised as 'not fit for purpose'. RBA rate warning pressures bank NIMs. Housing market stress threatens mortgage book quality.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from higher-for-longer rates and housing stress. Super fund managers (HUB.AX, PPA.AX) benefit from inflows but face policy disruption risk.

sectors.trend: Diesel/petrol shock rising; Sempra locks 20-year LNG demand; EV adoption accelerates in Australia. Oil weakness weighs on ASX via Wall Street transmission.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, SXG.AX face fuel demand headwinds from EV transition. LNG names (WDS.AX, GWO.AX) supported by long-term offtake. Oil-linked equities under pressure.

sectors.trend: Consumer weakness evident: Christmas retailer Chapter 11, 80-year discount chain closing 120 stores, Dollar General CEO flags red flags. Housing stress reduces consumer spending capacity.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX (retail), IAG.AX, and consumer discretionary names face headwinds. Defensive staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX) relatively resilient.

sectors.trend: AI slowdown warnings from Amodei, Altman, Musk; Anthropic delays IPO; OpenAI cash burn concerns. ASX small-caps Latrobe, CurveBeam, Arrow, Sultan lead weekly gains.
sectors.implications: ASML and semiconductor supply chain caution. ASX tech small-caps (LBR.AX, CRB.AX) show relative strength but liquidity risk. Global AI capex cycle may moderate.

sectors.trend: Sydney housing 'bloodbath', auction reality check, Intergenerational Report criticised. Higher rates suppress property valuations. Rental market disruption proposed.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICV.AX) face cap-rate expansion risk. Housing-linked equities (WBC.AX, CGW.AX) under pressure. Rental yield support possible from policy changes.

Iron ore structural downside vs. gold/critical minerals rotation
Super system reform debate: digital pension, contribution surges, fitness-for-purpose concerns
Consumer spending deterioration across retail and discretionary
Global risk-off: Buffett exit, 'four horsemen' warning, Trump trade war
EV transition accelerating in Australia, disrupting fuel demand
Housing market correction in Sydney with policy response uncertainty

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds, quality dividend payers; underweight rate-sensitive REITs and property developers
Reduce exposure to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; rotate into gold and critical minerals
Monitor bank NPLs; favour CBA.AX, NAB.AX over ANZ.AX, WBC.AX for credit quality; avoid property developers
Diversify away from export-concentrated names; favour domestic-revenue companies
Shift from discretionary to staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX); avoid retail exposure
Monitor WDS.AX, SXG.AX; consider EV supply chain beneficiaries

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight WA gold and critical minerals exploration names
opportunities.rationale: Forrestania four prefeasibility studies, Dalaroo Greenland rare earths, Larvotto antimony-gold, Great Southern 10.72g/t results signal sector momentum; iron ore rotation tailwind

opportunities.recommendation: Add quality dividend financials with strong credit books
opportunities.rationale: Higher rates support NIMs for well-capitalised banks; super inflows support fund managers; CBA/NAB best positioned for housing stress

opportunities.recommendation: Position in LNG long-term offtake beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: Sempra 20-year LNG deal signals structural demand; Australian LNG producers benefit from global energy security theme

Sydney housing bloodbath, auction reality check, higher rates expanding cap rates, Intergenerational Report credibility issues

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim consumer discretionary and retail exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Chapter 11 filings, store closures, consumer red flags indicate spending deterioration; shift to staples

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge global risk-off via quality defensives and cash
defensive_moves.rationale: Buffett exit, 'four horsemen' warning, Trump trade war, AI capex moderation signal elevated macro uncertainty

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure in 1-3 months. RBA rate decision imminent with hawkish bias. Iron ore weakness and global risk-off (Buffett exit, trade war) cap upside. Housing stress and consumer weakness weigh on financials and retail. Gold and critical minerals provide relative outperformance. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a range with downside bias.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive for selective sectors. Super reform and digital pension scheme may boost fund manager flows. LNG structural demand supports energy names. Gold/critical minerals benefit from diversification away from iron ore. Housing correction may stabilise by H2 2027. Key risk: prolonged global trade disruption and AI capex moderation.
key_catalysts: Iron ore price trajectory and Chinese stimulus response
watch_list: RBA cash rate and forward guidance
CBA.AX, NAB.AX NIM and credit metrics
US consumer spending data (Dollar General, retail bankruptcies)
